name: Germany

meta.title: Study in Germany from India: blocked account, fees, job search visa
meta.description: Public university fees in Germany, the €11,904 blocked account in rupees, winter and summer semester deadlines, student work limits and the 18-month job search permit.

summary: Low or no tuition at public universities, two semesters to start in, and 18 months to find a job after graduating.

whyReasons.text: Public universities charge no tuition for most bachelor's and master's programmes. Baden-Württemberg charges non-EU students €1,500 a semester.
After graduating in Germany you get up to 18 months to look for a job, and you may work during that time.
There are two starts a year: the winter semester (October) and the summer semester (April).

ug.note: Public universities: semester contribution of €70 to €430 per semester, plus tuition of €1,500 per semester in Baden-Württemberg. Bavarian universities may set their own fees. Private universities charge more.

pg.note: Same rules as bachelor's for most master's programmes at public universities. Some specialised master's charge fees.

living.note: DAAD's suggested budget for international students. For the visa you must show €992 a month (€11,904 a year), usually in a blocked account.

visaFunds.text: Proof of €992 a month (€11,904 for a year), usually through a blocked account, in effect since 1 January 2025.

applyBy.text: At most universities, apply between early May and 15 July.
At most universities, apply between early December and 15 January.

intakes.note: Private universities may have other deadlines.

duringStudy.text: Up to 120 full days or 240 half days of work a year.

afterStudy.text: A residence permit of up to 18 months to look for qualified work after graduating, if you can support yourself. You may take up any work during this time.

faq.q: Is studying in Germany really free?
faq.a: At most public universities there is no tuition for bachelor's and most master's courses. You still pay a semester contribution of €70 to €430. Baden-Württemberg charges non-EU students €1,500 a semester, and private universities charge full fees.

faq.q: How much goes into the blocked account?
faq.a: €992 a month, which is €11,904 for a year. You can draw the monthly amount after you arrive.
At most universities, 15 July for the winter semester and 15 January for the summer semester. Private universities may differ.

faq.q: Can I stay after my degree?
faq.a: Yes. You can get a residence permit for up to 18 months to look for work, and you may work during that time.
